verdict.rationale: Lium's SDK can rent the cheapest matching node, run a function there, return the result and remove the pod, which approximates scale-to-zero job execution (lium-docs-24). TTL and spend-cap auto-deletion and per-second billing (lium-docs-1, lium-docs-15, lium-docs-13) also avoid paying for always-on instances. However, this is ephemeral per-job pod rental, not a serverless worker or endpoint product: nothing shows request-driven autoscaling or managed worker pools. Missing for 10: autoscaling serverless endpoints or worker pools, request-driven scale-up/scale-down, a deploy-code-as-endpoint workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
